## Visual Studio Code and Copilot Ecosystem Updates

Franz provided an overview of recent updates in the Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, focusing on the introduction of Skills and improvements to context window management in Visual Studio Code, and discussed their implications for developers.

### MCP Servers and Context Window

Franz explained that MCP servers, introduced by Anthropic, allow large language models to interact with external tools via a common protocol, but their use can quickly fill the context window, leading to inefficiencies. To optimize, users are advised to enable only relevant MCP servers for their current tasks.

### Introduction of Skills

Franz described the new Skills feature as a simple, markdown-based mechanism for extending AI capabilities in Visual Studio Code. Skills can be created at the user or repository level, making them highly flexible and easy to share among team members.

### Context Window Usage Indicator

A new feature in Visual Studio Code Insiders displays a context window usage indicator, allowing users to monitor how much of the context window is being used and when to start a new conversation to avoid losing important information.

### Release Cadence and Availability

Franz clarified that Skills and the context window indicator are currently available in the VS Code Insiders track and will be released to the main version soon, addressing Casey's question about missing features in the standard release.

## Best Practices for Agents, Skills, and Instructions

Franz detailed the distinctions and best practices for using Agents MD, custom agents, skills, prompts, and instructions in Visual Studio Code, emphasizing the shift towards skills as the preferred method for extending AI functionality.

### Agents MD vs. Copilot Instructions

Franz recommended using Agents MD, an industry-standard markdown file, over Copilot Instructions for repository documentation, as it is supported by multiple tools and provides clear guidelines for large language models about the repository's structure and quirks.

### Custom Agents and Personas

Custom agents are described as persona-like configurations that encapsulate best practices or specialized roles, such as a testing agent or a coding agent, and can be applied at the user or repository level for consistent behavior across projects.

### Transition from Prompts and Instructions to Skills

Franz noted a personal shift from using repeatable prompts and custom instructions to relying almost exclusively on skills, as skills offer more flexibility and can encapsulate both instructions and executable scripts.

### User and Repository Scope

Most configuration files, except for Copilot Instructions and Agents MD, can be placed at the user level, making them reusable across multiple repositories and enhancing productivity.

## Technical Deep Dive into Skills Architecture

Franz provided an in-depth explanation of the skills architecture, including how skills are structured, discovered, and executed, and demonstrated their advantages over MCP servers through practical examples and audience questions from Zach.

### Skill Structure and Discovery

Skills are organized as folders containing a skill.md file with minimal front matter and optional scripts. The AI progressively discovers and loads only the necessary parts of a skill, minimizing context window usage and enabling efficient execution.

### Integration with Executable Scripts

Skills can reference and execute scripts such as PowerShell or Python, allowing deterministic operations like querying APIs or automating tasks, which enhances the AI's capabilities beyond static instructions.

### Comparison with MCP Servers

Unlike MCP servers, which always load their functions into context, skills are loaded on demand, allowing users to maintain hundreds or thousands of skills without overloading the context window.

### Practical Use Cases

Franz demonstrated skills for tasks such as generating images, querying Cortex and Azure DevOps APIs, and searching Slack, highlighting the ease of extending or creating new skills for specific workflows.

### Audience Q&A on Skills and MCP

In response to Zach's questions, Franz explained that skills can often replace MCP servers for most use cases, offering more power and flexibility, but MCP servers remain valid for users satisfied with their current setup.

## Managing Context Window and Chat Modes

Franz discussed strategies for managing the context window in Visual Studio Code, explained the different chat modes (ask, edit, plan, agent), and provided guidance on when to use each mode for optimal AI interactions.

### Context Window Management

Franz emphasized the importance of monitoring the context window to prevent loss of important information, suggesting users persist key facts in markdown files or use continuation prompts when nearing the context limit.

### Chat Modes Overview

The chat interface offers several modes: ask (safe, read-only, limited access), edit (single-file edits), plan (iterative planning with Q&A), and agent (full access to workspace and tools). Each mode serves different use cases and levels of control.

### Plan Mode Advantages

Plan mode encourages iterative clarification by prompting the AI to ask questions until a clear plan is established, reducing ambiguity and improving the quality of automated changes.

### Custom Agents in Chat

Custom agents defined in user or repository folders are available in the chat mode dropdown, allowing users to switch between different personas or specialized agents as needed.

## Organizational and Quality Assurance Agents

Franz described the use of organization-level agents, such as the C# quality expert, which provide automated quality assessments and recommendations for repositories, and explained how to enable these agents in Visual Studio Code.

### C# Quality Expert Agent

The C# quality expert agent evaluates repository quality across multiple grades, provides recommendations for improvement, and understands advanced topics like async patterns and linting, making it valuable for high-quality projects.

### Enabling Organization Agents

Users can opt into organization or enterprise agents via Visual Studio Code settings, which automatically provides access to specialized agents like the C# quality expert.
